t.E441.agn: In the EU, edible gelatine is not considered a food additive. In 1970 JECFA set the ADI as 'not limited'.
t.E441.eval: It is obtained from animal bones and skin; it may be of pig or cattle origin. Because in the EU it is considered a food rather than an additive, it is usually listed on the label as “gelatine” rather than by an E number.
t.E441.found.0: In the EU it is considered a food ingredient rather than an additive; used as a gelling agent and thickener in various foods
t.E441.prod: It is obtained by partial hydrolysis of animal collagen. Under EU legislation, its raw material may be bones, the skin of cattle and other farmed ruminants, pig skin, poultry skin, tendons, wild game skin, or fish skin and bones.
t.E441.pw.0: It is of animal origin (bone, skin, tendon or fish).
t.E441.pw.1: It is obtained from animal bone, skin or fish; it is not vegetarian.
t.E441.regx.0: Edible gelatine is not considered a food additive; E 441 is not in the EU list of additives.
t.E441.summary: A protein obtained from animal skin and bones (cattle, pig or fish). It forms a gel in Turkish delight, confectionery, jellies and some desserts.
t.E441.what: It forms a gel, thickens and keeps the mixture stable.
